correctness.rationale: Rechecked the final fixed-n extremal claim and its counting ingredient. For minima M(p) below p, pseudocomplement tests disjointness from the minima in the ideal, and double pseudocomplement tests all-inclusion. Comparable vertices have nested nonempty sets M(p), so gluing along paths makes the inclusion status constant across all minima of each component. Deleting the included minima realizes the factor 1+|J(C minus minima)|; the empty algebra representation has empty-product count one. A nonvalid component of size s with m>=2 minima has at most 1+2^(s-m) successes and at least 2^m-2 failures. The failure quotient is strictly monotone in the two counts in opposite directions, giving at least 2/(2^(s-2)+3). Equality forces m=2 and antihain structure on the remaining vertices, since every subset must be an ideal. A vertex lying above just one minimum would give a third failure by its principal ideal, so the two-level ordinal sum is forced, and direct count attains the bound. Probabilities factor across components; strict monotonicity of the size bound forces s=n in the equality case. This includes the first nonvalid size n=3. Frozen finite verifier and replay report were inspected, not rerun: all naturally labeled orders through size six (covering each isomorphism class), direct checks of extremizers through thirteen and structural checks through sixteen; these do not establish the universal claim.
